resources.string: GitHub limit reached (60 checks an hour): again after %1$s
Version of the apps to install: the one using LibreHU service, Jancar\'s ivi-services (stock ROM) or none. Apps with a single version ignore it.
No root: Android asks before each install (allow LibreHU Apps to install unknown apps)
Check once a day and notify
Replaced in /system: restart the head unit
The installed version was signed with another key (older builds each had their own). It must be uninstalled first: its settings are lost. Later updates install over it.
This app is installed in /system (privileged): it can also be replaced there as root, keeping its data; the head unit then has to restart.
No build kept on GitHub for this edition yet (the next build of the app adds them).
The last 15 builds of the edition are kept. Going back to an older one: Android only allows it by uninstalling first (or, as root, keeping the settings).
Changes unknown: the installed version does not say which commit it was built from.
Reading another app\'s logs needs root, or once from a computer: adb shell pm grant org.librehu.ota android.permission.READ_LOGS (then reopen LibreHU Apps).
No line from this app in Android\'s logs (they are cleared at each start, and only kept for a while).
Android refuses to install an older version over a newer one. Uninstall then install: the app\'s settings are lost.
With root its data can be kept (pm uninstall -k): if the newer version changed their format, the older one may not read them or may crash; uninstall it fully then.
This app is in /system: uninstalling only removes its update. If the /system copy is newer, put the older version in /system instead (Versions → Install in /system).
The app becomes a system app: it survives a reset to factory settings and, in /system/priv-app, gets the privileged permissions it asks for. Active after a restart of the head unit.
It asks for no privileged permission: /system/app is enough.
It asks for %1$d privileged permissions, only granted from /system/priv-app (added to Android\'s whitelist so that it still starts):
The version installed now is signed with another key: Android deletes it at the restart, its settings with it.

Later updates install over it, as for any system app. To remove it: the module in the root manager, or, written in /system, its folder in /system/app or /system/priv-app and its privapp-permissions file in /system/etc/permissions.
/system is read-only (%1$s): dm-verity, or the overlay of root modules. Install it as a module instead: same result, the partition stays untouched.
Module %1$s (recommended): mounted over /system at each start, the partition is not modified (works with dm-verity), removed from the modules list of %1$s.
No Magisk, KernelSU or APatch found: only writing in /system is possible (needs a /system that can be remounted read-write).
Official KernelSU 3.0 and later: modules only change /system with a metamodule (meta-overlayfs, from the KernelSU manager). KernelSU Next mounts them itself.
No configuration in the catalogue yet (configs of catalog.json).
The current file is copied to /sdcard/LibreHU/backup, then replaced: %1$s. Continue?
The zip is written to the internal storage and TWRP will flash it at the next start in recovery. Continue?

Configuration files (audio, CAN box, Jancar config…) and recovery zips. Root needed. A partition protected by dm-verity is never written: the head unit would not start (disable verity first with fastboot).
Put a file of the device
Choose the destination, then the file: the current one is saved first. A reboot may be needed for it to be used.
The zip is copied to the internal storage, TWRP\'s OpenRecoveryScript is written, then the head unit restarts in recovery: TWRP flashes it and restarts.
TWRP will flash the zip at the next start in recovery. Restart now?
Waiting for the installs before it…
Root only (nothing asks); LibreHU Apps itself last.
speed-profile, one app at a time: smooth from the first start (root).
%1$d app(s) set not to update (\"Do not update\" on their card).
Installs always run one after the other. Taken into account at the next start of the app.
A GitHub token without any scope raises the limit from 60 to 5000 requests per hour. Kept on the device, sent to api.github.com only.
Root. Updates (manual, \"update all\" and background) go to /system/priv-app or /system/app, as each app needs (privileged permissions), active after a reboot. LibreHU Apps itself stays in /data.
The new version runs without waiting for the reboot; /system has it from the next start (same signing key needed).
Flashable zips of LibreHU-flashablesZips, by category. Flashed by TWRP at the next start in recovery (TWRP needed: Recovery category); an image can also be written straight to its partition. Root.
Not for this device (%1$s; made for %2$s).
The zip is downloaded and checked (SHA-256), put in the internal storage, and TWRP will flash it at the next start in recovery. Continue?
The image is downloaded and checked, the current %1$s partition is copied to /sdcard/LibreHU/backup, then the image is written and read back. Continue?
A choice is needed: open LibreHU Apps
Progress, speed and time left, pause / resume, then installed or failed; also for the background installs.
No app in the catalogue yet
Check again with the button at the top right.
Downloads and installs show up here, with their progress.
LibreHU Apps installs and updates the LibreHU apps from their GitHub releases, and flashes the LibreHU zips.
With TWRP (restarts into the recovery now)

Android cannot write /system on this unit: the eMMC refuses the writes in a normal start (I/O error, write-protected regions of the stock kernel). Install it with TWRP: LibreHU Apps prepares a zip, restarts into the recovery, TWRP writes it and starts Android again.
